category: Output setup dialogs, Draftsman objects, ActiveBOM, multi-board & harness design, project history
description: Configuration dialogs for fabrication outputs (Gerber, NC Drill, Pick and Place), the Draftsman drawing objects, ActiveBOM features, multi-board schematic/assembly commands, harness design documents, Altium 365 project history and CAM editor operations.

tools.name: Gerber Setup > General tab
tools.description: Units (Inches or Millimeters) and Format (2:3, 2:4, 2:5 for inches; 4:2, 4:3, 4:4 for mm) that set the coordinate resolution of every Gerber file; higher formats are required for metric fine-pitch boards. The tab is the first page of the Gerber Setup dialog opened from File > Fabrication Outputs > Gerber Files or an OutJob Gerber output.
tools.usage: File > Fabrication Outputs > Gerber Files > General; OutJob > Fabrication Outputs > Gerber Files > Configure
tools.example: Millimeters, 4:4 for a 0.4 mm-pitch BGA board so 0.0001 mm resolution is preserved.
tools.notes: Gerber X2 output has its own setup with the same tabs plus attribute options.

tools.name: Gerber Setup > Layers tab
tools.description: Grid of all layers with Plot and Mirror checkboxes (Plot Layers menu: All On/Off/Used), a Mechanical Layers to Add to All Plots list (e.g. add the board outline mechanical layer to every film) and the Include unconnected mid-layer pads option. Determines which .GTL/.GBL/.G1/.GTO/.GTS/.GM1 files are produced.
tools.usage: Gerber Setup > Layers > Plot Layers > Used On; tick mechanical layers to add to all plots

parameters.name: Mechanical Layers to Add to All Plots
parameters.description: Overlay layers such as the outline on every film.

tools.example: Plot Layers > Used On, tick 'Mechanical 1 (Outline)' in the add-to-all list, untick Mirror everywhere.
tools.notes: Keep-Out Layer is never output; drill guide/drawing layers are handled on the Drill Drawing tab.

tools.name: Gerber Setup > Drill Drawing tab
tools.description: Enables Drill Drawing Plots and Drill Guide Plots per layer pair (Plot all used drill pairs, Mirror plots) and the drill symbol style (Graphic symbols, Size of hole string, Characters) and symbol size used in the drill drawing film (.GD1) and drill guide (.GG1).
tools.usage: Gerber Setup > Drill Drawing > Drill Drawing Plots / Drill Guide Plots > Plot all used drill pairs; Configure Drill Symbols

parameters.name: Drill Drawing Plots / Drill Guide Plots
Symbols
parameters.description: Graphic symbols | Size of hole string | Characters; symbol size.

tools.example: Enable Drill Drawing Plots for all used drill pairs with Graphic symbols 50 mil; the legend table appears where the Drill Table object or .Legend string is placed.
tools.notes: Draftsman drill tables are the modern alternative for documentation.

tools.name: Gerber Setup > Apertures tab
tools.description: Embedded apertures (RS274X) is the default and embeds the aperture list in each file; when disabled, a separate aperture (.apr/.apt) file is written and options appear for maximum aperture size, generating relief shapes, flash pad shapes and flash all fills. Leave embedded apertures on for all modern fabricators.
tools.usage: Gerber Setup > Apertures > Embedded apertures (RS274X)

parameters.name: Embedded apertures (RS274X)
parameters.description: Include aperture definitions in the Gerber files.

parameters.name: Max aperture size / Flash pad shapes / Flash all fills / Generate relief shapes

tools.example: Keep Embedded apertures enabled; no .apr file is produced and every .G* file is self-contained RS-274X.
tools.notes: RS274D output is obsolete; only use it if a legacy CAM system demands it.

tools.name: Gerber Setup > Advanced tab
tools.description: Film Size (X, Y, Border size), Aperture Matching Tolerances, Leading/Trailing Zeroes (Keep leading and trailing / Suppress leading / Suppress trailing), Position on Film (Reference to absolute origin / relative origin / Center on film), Batch Mode (Separate file per layer / Panelize layers), Plotter Type (Unsorted raster / Sorted vector), and Other options: G54 on aperture change, Use software arcs, Use polygons for octagonal pads, Generate DRC Rules export file (.RUL), Optimize change location commands.
tools.usage: Gerber Setup > Advanced

parameters.name: Film Size
parameters.description: Must exceed the board plus border or output is clipped.

parameters.name: Leading/Trailing Zeroes
parameters.description: Keep leading and trailing (recommended) | Suppress leading | Suppress trailing.

parameters.name: Position on Film
parameters.description: Reference to absolute origin | relative origin | Center on film.

parameters.name: Optimize change location commands
parameters.description: Shorter files; disable if a CAM tool misreads them.

tools.example: Film 20000 x 16000 mil, border 1000 mil, Keep leading and trailing zeroes, Reference to relative origin, Separate file per layer.
tools.notes: A 'board exceeds film size' error is fixed here by enlarging X/Y.

tools.name: NC Drill Setup dialog
tools.description: Options for Excellon drill files: Units (Inches/Millimeters) and Format (2:3/2:4/2:5 or 4:2/4:3/4:4), Leading/Trailing Zeroes (Suppress leading, Suppress trailing, Keep), Coordinate Positions (Reference to absolute or relative origin), Optimize change location commands, Generate separate NC Drill files for plated & non-plated holes, Generate Board Edge Rout Paths (with Rout Tool Dia), Generate EIA Binary Drill File (.DRL) and Generate DRR (Drill Report) file. Produces .TXT drill files per layer pair plus the .DRR report and .LDP layer-pair list.
tools.usage: File > Fabrication Outputs > NC Drill Files; OutJob > Fabrication Outputs > NC Drill Files > Configure

parameters.name: Generate Board Edge Rout Paths
parameters.description: Adds routing paths for the outline with a tool diameter.

tools.example: Millimeters 4:4, Keep leading and trailing zeroes, separate plated/non-plated, DRR enabled: files Board.TXT, Board-NPTH.TXT, Board.DRR.
tools.notes: Back drills and blind/buried pairs each produce their own drill file named by layer pair.

tools.name: Pick and Place Setup dialog
tools.description: Configures the component placement (centroid) file: output Formats (CSV, Text, Excel - one or several), Units (Imperial/Metric), the coordinate reference (board origin), and the column set and order (Designator, Footprint, Mid X, Mid Y, Ref X, Ref Y, Pad X, Pad Y, Layer, Rotation, Comment, plus component parameters); the OutJob's variant setting decides which fitted parts are listed. Generates 'Pick Place for <board>.csv/.txt/.xls'.
tools.usage: File > Assembly Outputs > Generates pick and place files; OutJob > Assembly Outputs > Generates pick and place files > Configure

parameters.name: Columns
parameters.description: Selected columns with Show checkbox and order.

tools.example: CSV, Metric, columns Designator, Mid X, Mid Y, Layer, Rotation, Footprint, Comment; generate per assembly variant from the OutJob.
tools.notes: Rotation follows Altium's convention (counter-clockwise, component origin); fabricators may need an offset file.

tools.name: Draftsman: Board Assembly View
tools.description: Automated composite of the board outline, cutouts, holes and component graphics (outlines, designators, pin-1 markers, 3D-body projections) from the top or bottom side, with per-view options for component display (Outline / Body / Graphic model), designator font, colour by variant, and layer content. Updates from the PCB via Tools > Update Board (or automatically when the PCB changes).
tools.usage: Draftsman document: Place > Board Assembly View; Properties: Side (Top/Bottom), Scale, Components display mode, Variant

parameters.name: Variant
parameters.description: Assembly variant to depict (not-fitted parts greyed/hidden).

tools.example: Place > Board Assembly View, set Side Top, Scale 2:1, Variant 'LowCost', then add a Bill Of Materials table for the same variant.
tools.notes: Board Detail Views and Callouts can be attached to it.

tools.name: Draftsman: Board Fabrication View
tools.description: Bare-board view (top or bottom) showing selected layers (copper, mask, silkscreen, mechanical, drill symbols) with per-layer colour/visibility settings, used for fabrication drawings and drill drawings; combined with a Drill Table and Layer Stack Legend.
tools.usage: Place > Board Fabrication View; Properties: Side, Scale, Layers list (visibility/colour), Drill symbols

parameters.name: Layers
parameters.description: Which board layers are drawn and in what colour.

parameters.name: Drill symbols
parameters.description: Show drill symbols keyed to the Drill Table.

tools.example: Board Fabrication View with Top Layer, Mechanical 1 and drill symbols; place Drill Table beside it.
tools.notes: For a plain drill drawing use the Drill Drawing View object.

tools.name: Draftsman: Board Section View and Board Detail View
tools.description: Board Section View creates a cross-section along a cut line drawn on a placed view (assembly, fabrication, isometric) showing layer stack, components and holes in profile, with section labels A-A; Board Detail View defines a circular/rectangular area on any supported view and creates a magnified floating copy with its own scale and label. Both keep referential links to the parent view.
tools.usage: Place > Board Section View (draw cut line on a view); Place > Board Detail View (draw detail region)

parameters.name: Cut line / detail area
parameters.description: Defined graphically on the parent view.

tools.example: Draw a section through the connector row to show component heights against the enclosure; add a detail view at 5:1 on the fine-pitch BGA.
tools.notes: Section views honour 3D bodies; components without bodies appear as flat outlines.

tools.name: Draftsman: Board Isometric View and Board Realistic View
tools.description: Board Isometric View projects the assembled board in an isometric (or custom-angle) line drawing; Board Realistic View embeds a scalable rendered 3D image of the board (as seen in the PCB 3D view) for cover sheets and assembly guides. Both accept variant selection and rotation settings.
tools.usage: Place > Additional Views > Board Isometric View / Board Realistic View
tools.example: Realistic view at 30/30 degrees on the title sheet; isometric line view with callouts on the assembly sheet.
tools.notes: Realistic views are raster images and increase PDF size.

tools.name: Draftsman: Board Region View, Component View, Counter Hole View, Drill Drawing View
tools.description: Additional views: Board Region View draws the layer-stack regions of a rigid-flex board with legends; Component View shows a single component (top/side) for detail notes; Counter Hole View documents counterbore/countersink hole profiles; Drill Drawing View is a bare outline with drill symbols only, for classic drill drawings.
tools.usage: Place > Additional Views > Board Region View | Component View | Counter Hole View | Drill Drawing View
tools.example: Drill Drawing View plus Drill Table and a Note listing hole tolerances on the fabrication sheet.
tools.notes: Counter holes are defined in the pad's hole properties on the PCB.

tools.name: Draftsman: Drill Table
tools.description: Automatically generated table of drill symbols, hole sizes, plated/non-plated state, tolerances, counts and layer pairs (one table per drill pair or combined), with configurable columns, units, symbol style and grouping (by size, by pair); synchronises with the Hole Size Editor data of the PCB.
tools.usage: Place > Drill Table; Properties: Columns, Units, Symbol style, Layer pair, Group by

parameters.name: Columns
parameters.description: Symbol, Hole Size, Tolerance, Plated, Count, Hole Type, Description.

tools.example: Drill Table for Top-Bottom pair plus a second table for the Top-L2 microvia pair beside the Board Fabrication View.
tools.notes: Hole tolerances come from the pad/via Hole Tolerance properties.

tools.name: Draftsman: Layer Stack Legend and Layer Stack Table
tools.description: Layer Stack Legend draws an enlarged sectional view of the stack (with layer names, materials, thicknesses, copper weights, Dk) as a graphic; Layer Stack Table presents the same data in tabular form with a region map for multi-stack boards. Both read the Layer Stack Manager and update automatically.
tools.usage: Place > Layer Stack Legend; Place > Layer Stack Table

parameters.name: Columns / Data
parameters.description: Name, Material, Type, Thickness, Weight, Dk, Df.

tools.example: Layer Stack Legend at 10:1 vertical scale with total thickness dimension on the fabrication sheet.
tools.notes: Replaces the legacy .Layer_Stack_Table special string on PCB mechanical layers.

tools.name: Draftsman: Bill Of Materials table and Transmission Line Table
tools.description: The Draftsman Bill Of Materials is an auto-generated table of assembly items sourced from the PCB or the project's ActiveBOM (BomDoc), with grouping, sorting, column selection (Line #, Designator, Quantity, Comment, Description, Footprint, MPN...), variant awareness and item-number linking to Callouts (balloons). Transmission Line Table lists impedance profiles with layer, width, gap and calculated impedance from the Layer Stack Manager.
tools.usage: Place > Bill Of Materials; Place > Transmission Line Table
tools.example: Place Bill Of Materials sourced from Board.BomDoc, group by Comment+Footprint, then Place > Callout on the assembly view with 'Component Item Number' to balloon each part.
tools.notes: Use the BomDoc source so the drawing BOM matches the released BOM output exactly.

tools.name: Draftsman: Callout, Note and Center Mark
tools.description: Annotation objects: Callout (leader pointing at a location or component, showing designator, item number, parameter or custom text, optionally auto-numbered from the BOM), Note (numbered text list block, referenced by note callouts), Center Mark (crosshair snapped to a hole/arc centre). Text supports special strings such as =ProjectName, =Revision.
tools.usage: Place > Callout | Note | Center Mark

parameters.name: Callout content
parameters.description: Designator | Item Number | Parameter | Custom text.

tools.example: Place > Note with fabrication notes 1-8; Place > Callout on the ESD diode with 'Note 3' reference.
tools.notes: Callouts attached to components follow them when the PCB is updated.

tools.name: Draftsman: GD&T annotations (Datum Feature, Surface Finish, Feature Control Frame)
tools.description: Geometric dimensioning and tolerancing objects: Datum Feature (datum letter attached to an edge/hole), Surface Finish symbol per ISO 1302:2002 with roughness parameters, and Feature Control Frame (tolerance type, value, modifiers, datum references) for position/flatness callouts on mechanical drawings.
tools.usage: Place > Datum Feature | Surface Finish | Feature Control Frame
tools.example: Datum A on the left board edge, Datum B on the bottom edge, Feature Control Frame Position 0.1 |A|B on the mounting holes.
tools.notes: Standard drawing frames/title blocks come from Draftsman document templates.

tools.name: Draftsman: Dimensions (Linear, Radial, Diametral, Angular, Ordinate, X,Y Axis Scale)
tools.description: Associative dimensions that snap to edges, holes and arcs of Draftsman views and update with the board: Linear (between two points/edges), Radial (arc radius), Diametral (hole diameter), Angular (between two faces), Ordinate (running dimensions from a datum origin), and X,Y Axis Scale (a ruler/scale reference next to a view). Properties: units, precision, tolerance text, arrow style.
tools.usage: Place > Dimension > Linear | Radial | Diametral | Angular | Ordinate; Place > X,Y Axis Scale
tools.example: Ordinate dimensions from the lower-left board corner to every mounting hole on the fabrication view.
tools.notes: Dimension defaults are set in Draftsman document properties (Preferences > Draftsman).

tools.name: Draftsman document templates and sheet setup
tools.description: Draftsman documents (.PCBDwf) can start from a document template (sheets, title block, border, predefined views and tables with special strings) or a sheet template; templates are created by saving a Draftsman document as a template and are managed locally or in the Workspace (Preferences > Data Management > Templates). Document properties set sheet size, units, default fonts, line styles and the source PCB/variant.
tools.usage: Project > Add New to Project > Draftsman Document > choose template; Properties panel (no selection) for sheet/document settings; File > Save As template

parameters.name: Source PCB / Variant
parameters.description: Board and variant the views reference.

tools.example: Create 'Company_Fab_Assy' template with two sheets (fabrication with Board Fabrication View, Drill Table, Layer Stack Legend; assembly with Board Assembly View and BOM) and reuse it on every project.
tools.notes: Draftsman drawings update through Tools > Update Board or automatically when the PCB changes.

tools.name: ActiveBOM: BOM Checks (warnings and errors)
tools.description: The BOM Checks region of the BomDoc lists violations detected against configurable severities (Warning/Error/No Report) in the BOM Checks dialog: e.g. Component has no manufacturer part choice, Manufacturer part is not found by supplier, Supplier part number invalid, Part lifecycle Obsolete/NRND, Insufficient stock for production quantity, Price not available, Design item ID mismatch, Component revision not latest, Alternative part not defined. Errors can block the Project Releaser.
tools.usage: ActiveBOM document > BOM Checks panel region > gear icon (BOM Checks dialog) > Report Mode per check

parameters.name: Report mode
parameters.description: No Report | Warning | Error per check.

tools.example: Set 'No manufacturer part chosen' to Error so every line must have a solution before release.
tools.notes: Checks are evaluated live against supplier data from Parts Providers.

tools.name: ActiveBOM: Solutions, part choices ranking and Custom items
tools.description: Each BOM line shows Solutions built from the component's Part Choices with supplier offers ranked by availability, price and lifecycle; the Solution column lets you choose the manufacturer part and supplier, add a manufacturer part choice from the Manufacturer Part Search, or mark 'No part choice'. Custom items (bare PCB, screws, glue, labels) are added with Add Custom Item and carry their own quantity/MPN/price so the BOM is complete for purchasing.
tools.usage: ActiveBOM > right-click line > Solutions / Add Part Choice; toolbar > Add Custom Item; Properties panel > Supply Chain (Solutions per Item, Suppliers per Solution, Favorite Suppliers)

parameters.name: Solutions per Item / Suppliers per Solution
Production Quantity / Currency
parameters.description: Basis for stock and cost calculations.

tools.example: Set Production Quantity 500, add custom item 'PCB fab' qty 1, resolve red lines by picking in-stock solutions, export via the BOM output.
tools.notes: Solutions are saved in the BomDoc and used by the BOM output's supply-chain columns.

tools.name: ActiveBOM: columns, Design Item ID grouping and line numbers
tools.description: The Properties panel's Columns tab selects and orders columns (Design Item ID, Designator, Quantity, Comment, Description, Footprint, Manufacturer, Manufacturer Part Number, Supplier, Supplier Part Number, Unit Price, Stock, Lifecycle, Status, Line #, custom parameters) and drag-to-group columns; grouping by Design Item ID (or Comment+Footprint for file-based parts) consolidates identical parts into one line. Line numbers are assigned (Line # column) and locked so numbering stays stable across revisions.
tools.usage: ActiveBOM > Properties panel > Columns (Show, Group by drag area); BOM Items area > right-click > Line numbers

parameters.name: Group by
parameters.description: Columns dragged into the grouping area.

parameters.name: Line #
parameters.description: Stable BOM line numbering used by Draftsman callouts.

tools.example: Group by Design Item ID and Footprint, show Quantity, MPN, Unit Price, Lifecycle; the Draftsman BOM and BOM output inherit this layout.
tools.notes: Quantity 'As Required' appears for wire/cable/harness items.

tools.name: BOM templates (Excel .xlt/.xlsx, BomDoc templates) and Report Manager options
tools.description: BOM outputs (Reports > Bill of Materials or OutJob Report Outputs > Bill of Materials) can use an Excel template whose Field= and Column= placeholders are filled with BOM data, giving corporate formatting; templates are chosen in the Report Manager (Template field, Export options: file format XLS/XLSX/CSV/TXT/PDF/HTML/XML, Add to Project, Open Exported, Relative Path to Template). ActiveBOM templates (.BomDoc templates) preset columns/grouping for new BomDocs and are managed in Data Management > Templates.
tools.usage: Reports > Bill of Materials > Properties (General/Columns/Export options) > Template; Preferences > Data Management > Templates for BomDoc templates

parameters.name: Export format
parameters.description: XLS | XLSX | CSV | TXT | PDF | HTML | XML.

tools.example: Choose BOM_Company.xlsx template (columns Line #, Qty, MPN, Manufacturer, Designators), export XLSX per variant from the OutJob.
tools.notes: Sample templates ship in <Documents>\Altium\ADxx\Templates.

tools.name: Multi-board Schematic (*.MbsDoc): Modules and connections
tools.description: Logical system document of a multi-board project (.PrjMbd) where each child PCB project is placed as a Module (Designator, Title, Source project) whose entries are the project's connectors; modules are linked with Direct Connection, Cable or Harness connection objects, and wires/buses. Design > Import From Child Projects pulls connector/pin data and Design > Run ERC checks pin-to-pin compatibility, with mismatches resolved through the Connection Manager (net name conflicts, pin swaps).
tools.usage: Project > Add New to Project > Multi-board Schematic; Place > Module; Place > Direct Connection / Cable / Harness; Design > Import From Child Projects; Design > Run ERC; Design > Connection Manager
tools.example: Place modules MCU_Board and IO_Board, connect J3 to J1 with a Cable connection, Import From Child Projects, Run ERC, open Connection Manager to fix a swapped RX/TX pair by Swap Pins and push changes to the child project via ECO.
tools.notes: Child projects must be compiled and their connectors flagged (Connector component type / Multi-board connector parameter) to appear as entries.

tools.name: Multi-board Assembly (*.MbaDoc): import, mating, collision check
tools.description: Physical counterpart of the multi-board schematic: Design > Update Assembly imports each child PCB (with 3D bodies) and STEP enclosures (Design > Insert STEP Part), the Multiboard Assembly panel lists the parts tree, Tools > Mating aligns connectors by picking mating faces/points, Tools > Check Collisions reports intersecting surfaces in the Messages panel, and sections/exploded views feed Draftsman Multiboard Views. The assembly can be exported as STEP/Parasolid for MCAD.
tools.usage: Project > Add New to Project > Multi-board Assembly; Design > Update Assembly; Design > Insert STEP Part; Tools > Mating; Tools > Check Collisions; File > Export > STEP

parameters.name: Mating
parameters.description: Pairs of faces/points on two boards to align.

tools.example: Update Assembly, mate the mezzanine connector to the main-board socket, Check Collisions: a capacitor under the mezzanine intersects - move it on the child PCB and re-import.
tools.notes: Requires accurate 3D bodies on both boards; board-to-board connectors should have STEP models.

tools.name: Harness Wiring Diagram (*.WirDoc)
tools.description: Harness design project (.PrjHar) document where connectors, splices and No Connect markers are placed and joined with harness wires and cables (twisted pairs, shielded cables) to define electrical connectivity; connectors are placed from managed harness components. Wire properties include gauge, colour, length and part; the document feeds the Layout Drawing and BOM.
tools.usage: Project > Add New to Project > Harness Wiring Diagram; Place > Connector | Splice | Harness Wire | Cable | No Connect

parameters.name: Connector part
parameters.description: Managed harness connector component with pins.

tools.example: Place J1 (10-pin) and J2, draw harness wires pin 1-1, 2-2 with 22 AWG red/black, add a splice for the shared ground.
tools.notes: Harness Design requires the System.HarnessDesignAvailable advanced setting in early releases (AD 24+ has it enabled).

tools.name: Harness Layout Drawing (*.LdrDoc)
tools.description: Physical construction document of the harness: Design > Import Wiring Diagram brings the connectors and wires in; connectors are placed as physical model views, wires are grouped into Harness Bundles routed between Connection Points/nodes, and bundle lengths, breakouts and protection (sleeving) are dimensioned. Wire lengths computed here become the BOM's As Required quantities.
tools.usage: Project > Add New to Project > Harness Layout Drawing; Design > Import Wiring Diagram; Place > Harness Bundle | Connection Point; Properties for bundle length/protection

parameters.name: Bundle
parameters.description: Group of wires between two connection points with length.

tools.example: Import wiring diagram, place J1 at (0,0) and J2 at (500,0), draw a bundle with a breakout to J3 at 300 mm, dimension bundle lengths.
tools.notes: Extension is .LdrDoc (Layout Drawing); harness Draftsman documents use .HarDwf.

tools.name: Harness Draftsman document (*.HarDwf): Wiring List, Connection Table, Layout Drawing View
tools.description: Manufacturing drawing for a harness containing read-only Wiring Diagram View and Layout Drawing View objects, a harness Bill Of Materials, a Wiring List (start/end points, wire part, length, colour per wire) and Connection Tables (wires connected to every pin of each connector), plus callouts, notes and dimensions. Generated to PDF through the harness OutJob; Validate Harness Project checks the design first.
tools.usage: Project > Add New to Project > Draftsman Document (in .PrjHar); Place > Wiring Diagram View | Layout Drawing View | Wiring List | Connection Table | Bill Of Materials; Project > Validate Harness Project
tools.example: Sheet 1: Layout Drawing View with bundle dimensions; Sheet 2: Wiring List and Connection Tables for J1-J3; publish PDF via the OutJob.
tools.notes: Harness components (connectors, wires, cables, splices) are managed components with harness-specific parameters.

tools.name: Project History (Altium 365)
tools.description: Timeline view of a Workspace project showing every commit (with author, message, changed documents), release, clone, and comment event; each commit can be opened in the web viewer, compared visually with another (schematic/PCB diff), downloaded, or restored. Opened from the Projects panel (right-click project > History) or the Altium 365 web interface.
tools.usage: Projects panel > right-click project > History; Altium 365 web > project > History
tools.example: Open History, select commits #14 and #16, click Compare to see which nets changed in the schematic diff.
tools.notes: Requires the project to be under Workspace version control (Save to Server / Commit).

tools.name: Save to Server / Commit and Push (Workspace version control)
tools.description: For Workspace-hosted projects, changed documents are committed with Project > Save to Server (Git-based Workspaces: Commit, then Push) with a commit message; Project > Refresh/Pull retrieves others' changes, and Project > Show Differences / History give diffs. Legacy SVN/Git repositories configured in Design Repositories use the Storage Manager panel for commit/update.
tools.usage: Project > Save to Server (or right-click project > Save to Server); Project > Refresh from Server; Storage Manager panel for SVN/Git repos

parameters.name: Documents
parameters.description: Checklist of modified files to include.

tools.example: Finish routing, Project > Save to Server, message 'Route DDR bank 0', OK: the commit appears in Project History and the web viewer.
tools.notes: Conflicts on the same document are detected on save; Altium locks are advisory - coordinate via Comments.

tools.name: CAM Editor: import, netlist extraction, DRC and panelization (CAMtastic)
tools.description: The CAMtastic-based CAM editor (.Cam document) imports Gerber/ODB++/NC drill/IPC-D-356 data (File > Import), extracts a netlist from the copper (Tools > Netlist > Extract), compares it with an IPC-D-356 netlist, runs manufacturing DRC (Analysis > DRC/DFM), creates step-and-repeat panels and re-exports Gerber/ODB++/drill files after edits such as adding fiducials or step-and-repeat arrays.
tools.usage: File > New > CAM Document; File > Import > Gerber / ODB++ / Drill; Tools > Netlist > Extract; Analysis > DRC; Tables > Layers; File > Export > Gerber

parameters.name: Layer type assignment
parameters.description: Tables > Layers to classify imported files (top, bottom, mask, drill...).

parameters.name: DRC rules
parameters.description: Minimum spacing/annular ring checks in Analysis > DRC.

tools.example: Import the generated Gerbers and NC drill, run Tools > Netlist > Extract and Analysis > Compare Netlists against the IPC-D-356 export to confirm the outputs match the design.
tools.notes: Output verification only; edits in CAM are not reflected back into the PcbDoc.
